answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments act as a cryptographic prism, refracting history into non-malleable, succinct proofs of state. These primitives mirror the sequential hardness of delay functions, rendering identity cloning computationally infeasible against parallelized attacks. Such unforgeability ensures that a comet of malicious spoofing attempts cannot breach the Byzantine fault tolerance threshold or compromise the information-theoretic security of the network.
